newsitem.title: USA: Showers seen slowing U.S. HRW wheat harvest - WSC.
newsitem.headline: Showers seen slowing U.S. HRW wheat harvest - WSC.

text.p: Showers look set to slow harvesting of U.S. hard red winter wheat later Tuesday, particularly from central Kansas southward into Oklahoma, Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio said.

"We do expect to see showers and thunderstorms expand to include much of the winter wheat areas today, tonight and continuing on Wednesday," he said, noting the central Kansas to Oklahoma area would receive 0.50 to 2.00 inches of rain.
Burgio said during the last 12 hours there had been scattered thunderstorms on the fringe of the wheat belt in eastern Kansas and southeast Nebraska.
In northern Kansas rainfall was expected to be lighter.
"There is a slight chance of a few scattered showers of up to 0.50 inch or so (in northern Kansas) but not as much as the central and southern areas," Burgio said.
Weekly state crop reports, issued Monday, showed the Kansas wheat harvest was 67 percent complete, as of Sunday, with the Oklahoma harvest 91 percent done.

In Nebraska, where the wheat harvest was only three percent complete, mostly light showers are seen developing in the west later Tuesday. The southeast has already been soaked with Grand Island receiving 1.15 inches of rain.
